newsitem.title: UK: Dated Brent improves slightly but direction hazy.
newsitem.headline: Dated Brent improves slightly but direction hazy.

text.p: The value of Dated Brent was marginally higher after an early October Brent was sold at November evens but market direction was uncertain with the seller still holding a further 4.0 million barrels of Brent.

The cash market was quiet with no paper deals heard done except for a CFD roll done at +1 cent for a Sept 25-27 date and this week's dates done at a firmer Nov +2 cents against earlier bids at Nov -3.
Paper spreads also firmed with Oct/Nov done at +42 cents during the afternoon. Nov/Dec was talked at +43/+47 and Dec/Jan at +52/+55.

The oil major holding 4.0 million barrels of Brent kept the one Oct 8-10 Brent which turned wet on Monday. It later sold the Oct 4-6 cargo after turning down an offer of Nov -5 cents for a VLCC load, traders said.
"November flat seems to be a fair value for Brent," the seller said.
A trader also sold an end Sept/early Oct Brent cargo at an unknown price.
Some traders were uncertain as to the lure of Brent at such levels with scant refiner interest for the lighter end of the barrel and the transatlantic arbitrage still unworkable.
A trader said talk was firmer on the gas oil rich grades like Oseberg but no new deals were heard on other North Sea crudes.
In the Med, Urals was offered at Dated -65 cents by sellers confident of higher numbers in a tight sour market.
Traders said this was more than 10 cents up on the last done deal in the high 70s when a refiner picked up 130,000 tonnes last week.
"It is total death in the sour market. There is very little to move. There is virtually no September Urals left and we are expecting early October barrels to show," a trader said.
